study type: Cross-sectional study with a 2-week follow-up for neonatal body composition.
exposure: DNA methylation status of ATG2B, NKX6.1, SLC13A5, and GPR120 genes in placenta and cord blood
outcome: Neonatal body composition (total and abdominal fat at age 2 weeks)
Gene expression levels (ATG2B, NKX6.1, SLC13A5, GPR120)
cohort: The study included placentas and cord blood from term infants born either appropriate-for-gestational-Age (AGA) or small-for-gestational-Age (SGA).
finding: Alterations in methylation and expression of genes involved in energy homeostasis (ATG2B, NKX6.1, SLC13A5, GPR120) were significantly associated with fetal growth status and neonatal body composition.
followup_time: 2 weeks after birth (for neonatal body composition assessment)
cross-section timing: Placental and cord blood analyses were performed at birth, and neonatal body composition was assessed at 2 weeks of age.
birth_weight: The study included infants categorized as appropriate-for-gestational-Age (AGA) or small-for-gestational-Age (SGA), which implies a range of birth weights relative to gestational age.
